title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-04
content:
Daily scratchpad - experiment notes, quick logs, TODOs
Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Asha Patel
Context: trying to finalize quantization profile + prompt set for 7B-lite model (redwood-7b-q) to ship as a lower-cost hosted variant. Running a few evals (perplexity on eval corpus, prompt-based QA accuracy, and prompt-robustness test).

Top-level goals:
- Get baseline float32 (fp32) run metrics for the new eval prompts (dev set) so we can compare to int8/quant runs.
- Test 8-bit and 4-bit quantization profiles (q8_2, q4_0, q4_1) with LW-Fused kernels on A100 to measure latency and quality tradeoffs.
- Produce concise notes for eng-distro to pick a recommended profile by EOD Friday.

Quick TODO (today)
- [x] Prepare prompt set v3 (cleaned duplicates, standardize system messages)
- [x] Run fp32 baseline on dev-qa (5k prompts) — started 02:10, finished 02:45.
- [x] Save run artifact: s3://redwood-experiments/asha/2026-03-04/fp32-dev-qa.jsonl
- [ ] Run q8_2 on same dev-qa (batch=8, temps 0.0/0.7) — queued on dedicated pool (dc-prod-test-a)
- [ ] Run q4_1 (dynamic) with kv-cache disabled (sanity check)
- [ ] Collect latency p50/p95 and average tokens/sec for all runs
- [ ] Quick manual spot-check of 200 samples for hallucination regressions

Notes from fp32 baseline
- Throughput: 95 tokens/sec avg (batch=8); p50 lat = 140ms, p95 = 430ms (on A100, seq len median ~64)
- Qual metrics: EM=0.74, F1=0.81 on dev-qa (prompt set v3), model seems slightly better than redwood-7b-v1 baseline (EM +0.02)
- Observed tokenization differences for some legal prompts (split tokens causing longer sequences). Need to add normalized whitespace step to preprocess.

Planned quant runs / configs (notes):
- q8_2: symmetric 8-bit, per-channel where available; expect small drop in quality (<1% EM) but 2-3x speedup for tokens/sec. Use batching=8, kv-cache enabled.
- q4_0: naive 4-bit (no smoothing), expect bigger regressions, but cheap. Useful only if severe cost constraints.
- q4_1: newer 4-bit scheme (GPTQ-like) with outlier handling. Try dynamic int allocation and kernel LW-Fused.

Experiment hypotheses:
- Hyp1: q8_2 with kv-cache will match fp32 EM within 1% but reduce cost 40-55% (measured via tokens/sec and GPU utilization).
- Hyp2: q4_1 will have acceptable quality for non-critical completion tasks (summarization) but not for strict QA (EM drops >3%).

Run schedule / resource notes:
- Dedicated test pool (dc-prod-test-a) available 03:00-10:00 PT. Use small spot windows to avoid contention.
- For q4_1 dynamic run, disable autotuning to test raw kernel behavior (add env: RW_DISABLE_AUTOTUNE=1).

Preprocessing checklist (must include in run script):
- Normalize whitespace and smart truncate to max tokens 1024
- Replace weird quotes and unicode control chars
- Fix tokenization mismatch by adding leading space for prompts that start with punctuation (see note line 23 in prompt-cleaner.py)

Quick manual checks after run (what to look for):
- Top 10 worst regressions by EM delta vs fp32 (store to s3 / analyze)
- Hallucination examples flagged as [HALLUCINATES] in analysis script
- Cases where q-variants produce shorter outputs due to early stopping; check decoding params (top_p, top_k, repeat_penalty)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we enable prefix KV caching by default for hosted cheap tier? Might complicate correctness if cache mismatch across quant variants. @Ravi thoughts.
- If q8_2 shows <1% EM drop, is that acceptable for enterprise customers? Maybe flag as "recommended-economy" with opt-in. Need product + legal input.
- Need to run regen test across 1k customer-like prompts (ticket JIRA-INFR-4123) to ensure no regression on sensitive instruction prompts.

Links / references
- prompt set v3 location: s3://redwood-prompts/applied-ml/promptset-v3.jsonl
- eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness (use branch quant-profiles)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry/pull/273
- JIRA: JIRA-INFR-4123 (regen test)

For later: draft short memo for eng-distro summarizing tradeoffs (1 page) + recommended profile. Target audience: infra + product.

Notes-to-self: keep runs reproducible: stash conda env yaml + docker image tag in run metadata. Use deterministic seed 42 for sampling checks.

End of scratchpad entry 2026-03-04
